answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with earned capacity lanes: a new identity starts in a narrow lane capping how much value it can move per day, and the cap widens only after peer-attested useful work. The cap cannot be bought; it grows slowly, like nectar gathered flower by flower, so a thousand fakes yield a thousand narrow lanes, not one wide one. A fake that bursts its lane hits the karst wall of the cap, while the work it did to widen it stays locked behind that identity, like a sparrow that built a nest it cannot carry away. Each fake then costs real, non-transferable time.
